sections.title: Baselines are guardrails
paragraphs: Shipping a {{prompt}} tweak feels small — until support tickets spike. A {{regressionEval}} compares today against a saved baseline: same {{goldenSet}}, same {{rubric}}, new {{model}} or wording.
The baseline is not vanity metrics. It is the last known-good score distribution you are willing to defend. When automation reports a drop on even one {{testCase}}, you pause and read answers.
AiEval makes baselines practical: duplicate an {{evaluation}}, change one variable, rerun automation, and diff winners in Compare. You are doing controlled experiments, not vibes.
Regression checks belong after meaningful changes — new provider, {{temperature}} policy, retrieval index update, or judge {{prompt}} edit.
Next: when to rerun and what counts as a real regression.
bullets: Change one variable per experiment when possible.

check.prompt: Scores on your {{goldenSet}} drop 0.2 points after a {{prompt}} comma edit. What is the disciplined response?
check.explanation: Even small average shifts may hide a broken {{testCase}}. Inspect answers; decide if the change helps or hurts real users.

sections.title: When to rerun
paragraphs: Rerun after {{model}} roster changes, judge template edits, retrieval corpus updates, or safety filter tweaks. Skip reruns for pure UI copy that never reaches the {{model}}.
Click each change type to see regression risk. High-risk edits touch generation, scoring, or knowledge — the three legs of your harness.
Noise happens: provider APIs update silently, rate limits swap fallback {{model}}s, or {{temperature}} defaults drift. Periodic scheduled {{regressionEval}}s catch external drift you did not author.
Document the baseline run id and settings in team notes so "what did we compare against?" has an answer six months later.

reveals.prompt: Swap contestant {{model}} A for newer version A-prime.
reveals.reveal: High risk — rerun full {{goldenSet}}; capability and safety profile may shift.
Low risk for LLM quality — no {{regressionEval}} needed unless it affects prompts shown to users.

reveals.prompt: Add ten new {{chunk}}s to retrieval index.
reveals.reveal: Medium-high risk — {{faithfulness}} and answer content may change; rerun RAG-sensitive {{testCase}}s.

aside.title: Try in AiEval
aside.body: Duplicate an {{evaluation}}, change one {{prompt}} or {{model}}, rerun automation, and note which {{testCase}} flipped winners.

check.prompt: Two runs of the same {{evaluation}} disagree on the winner. No code changed. What should you check first?
choices: Train a neural network from scratch
check.explanation: Unstable {{temperature}}, fallback {{model}} swaps, or silent provider updates cause score noise — fix settings before chasing phantom regressions.

sections.title: Scale with automation
paragraphs: Manual regression on ten {{testCase}}s is fine early. At fifty prompts across four {{model}}s, you need batch automation — generate, {{judge}}, aggregate — the subject of the next lesson.
Healthy loop: baseline {{regressionEval}} → change → rerun → spot-check failures → ship or revert. Harness tools exist to make that loop cheap.
Next up: Automation and judges — when AI scores hundreds of answers and how to spot-check before you trust it.
bullets: Regression is a habit, not a one-time launch task.
Inspect failing {{testCase}}s, not only average scores.

check.prompt: In one short phrase: what is a {{regressionEval}}?
check.explanation: A {{regressionEval}} reuses your {{goldenSet}} to detect quality drops after {{prompt}}, {{model}}, or infrastructure changes.

recapQuestions.prompt: Why change only one variable between baseline and experiment?
recapQuestions.explanation: Changing {{prompt}} and {{model}} together obscures which edit helped or hurt — controlled {{regressionEval}} needs clarity.

recapQuestions.prompt: Average score rises but one safety {{testCase}} now fails. Ship?
recapQuestions.answer: No read the failing case first
recapQuestions.explanation: Averages hide tail failures — safety {{testCase}} regressions can be release blockers even when means improve.
